scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

F-02.statement: 1,785 disputed bills are on ACTUAL read type.

F-03.statement: billing-db tariff_change_log contains 0 records in the relevant period.

F-04.statement: Field route completion for 9,200 manual-read accounts was 0.88 against a 0.95 target over period 2026-08..09.

F-05.statement: crm-tickets dispute_response_times: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days, across 2,440 tickets.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-HANDLING.statement: The dispute surge is mainly a ticket-response throughput/handling problem; auto-answering tickets with an AI agent would bring volume back to baseline.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August caused incorrect bill calculations, driving the dispute increase.

H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE.statement: The AMI/MDMS nightly export pipeline (H-MDMS-BILL) degraded or dropped reads around August, forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-QUALITY.statement: Manual field meter reads passed via H-FIELD-BILL contain invalid or erroneous values that are feeding directly into wrong bills.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A field staffing shortfall left manual-read routes incomplete, increasing 'no accepted read' estimate substitutions and bill errors.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTION.statement: Billing import rejects AMI reads flagged as high-consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution and explaining 1,184 of the 1,240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills (E-12).

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db shows disputed bills split 1,240 ESTIMATED vs 1,785 ACTUAL read type, so the majority of the 3,025 disputed bills are on bills built from ACTUAL (not estimate-substituted) reads. This narrows the causal space away from pure estimate-substitution failures (export outage, missed routes) and toward problems that also/mainly hit actual-read billing, e.g. erroneous actual reads or a calculation/rule change applied broadly.

E-01 still shows the billing-db count split of 1,240 ESTIMATED vs 1,785 ACTUAL disputed bills (F-01, F-02); that raw count observation stands. It no longer supports a clean two-track causal story that routes ESTIMATED-type disputes to estimate-substitution/staffing while ACTUAL-type reflects read-quality: E-12 shows 1,184 of the 1,240 ESTIMATED bills actually had legitimate AMI reads rejected at import, the same import-validation failure mode, so E-01's split no longer separates distinct causal mechanisms.

billing-db's tariff_change_log returns zero records, meaning no tariff rate changes were logged around the dispute surge window; this rules out a tariff-rate change as the mechanism behind incorrect bill amounts, but it does not speak to import validation rule changes, read quality, AMI exports, field staffing, or ticket-response handling.

Route-log shows manual-read route completion for the 9,200 manual-read accounts was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026, meaning roughly 1,100 manual-read accounts did not get a completed route visit in that window — a real but partial shortfall, not a near-total breakdown.

E-03 still shows the raw route-completion observation: 88% completion against a 95% target for 9,200 manual-read accounts over Aug-Sep 2026, i.e. roughly 1,100 accounts without a completed visit. It no longer supports that this shortfall is the mechanism feeding the ESTIMATED-type disputed bills: E-12 shows only 56 of the 1,240 ESTIMATED disputes had no read received, while 1,184 had reads received but rejected at import, so the route-completion gap explains at most a small fraction of the ESTIMATED-type share.

crm-tickets shows median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2,440 tickets, meaning dispute response handling is currently fast and within SLA, not slow. This undercuts the premise that slow ticket-response handling is driving the dispute surge, since response speed looks adequate rather than degraded.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (role: Field Operations Manager, stated incentive: contract headcount increase, stated bias: attributes problems to staffing) claims a 3-reader shortfall since July causes routes to run late, resulting in estimated bills for affected customers. This is an unverified claim offering a candidate mechanism for the route-completion shortfall already observed in E-03 (88% vs 95% target), but by its own content it only explains ESTIMATED-type billing, not the majority ACTUAL-read disputes shown in E-01.

E-05 still shows the raw stakeholder claim: SH-FIELD, an interested, non-authoritative source, asserts a 3-reader shortfall since July causing late routes and estimated bills. It no longer plausibly explains the ESTIMATED-type disputed-bill majority mechanism: E-12 shows 1,184 of 1,240 ESTIMATED disputes had reads received but rejected at import (not missed routes), so the staffing claim's causal link to the ESTIMATED-type dispute share is now unsupported.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states there has been no tariff change this year; this is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim that corroborates the already-authoritative E-02 finding (billing-db tariff_change_log: 0 records) ruling out a tariff-rate change as a bill-amount error mechanism.

crm-tickets' monthly dispute volume (610, 590, 1180, 1260 for Jun-Sep 2026) authoritatively confirms the surge described in the initial request: volume held near 600/month through July then roughly doubled in August and stayed elevated through September. The jump is a sharp one-month step change rather than a gradual rise, which is more consistent with a sudden triggering event in the July/August window than a slow attrition-driven drift.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: This document establishes that route priority changes (push_route_update) may be requested by the utility but are only executed after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD), confirming the authority chain already encoded in constraint K-DISPATCH rather than revealing a new causal mechanism.

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db shows 320 accounts received an estimated bill last cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes, with only account_id and route fields returned (no dispute status, error type, or read-source data). This is targeting data for the pending push_route_update action but does not itself establish a causal mechanism for disputed bills or resolve any open unknown about read-error source or rule-change contribution.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

problem_definition.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1,220/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07). structural_remedies.description: Query billing-config rule-change log (DA-RULES) to check whether an import validation rule change around August caused incorrect ACTUAL-read calculations, closing VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONTRIBUTION.
structural_remedies.rationale: This is already in intended_scope (review_rule_change_log:DA-RULES), is a read-only deterministic query, and billing-config has AUTHORITATIVE status with no reported access blocker, so it is achievable within the 225-minute remaining budget.; residual gap: Only answers the rule-change question; does not identify or fix the manual/AMI read-quality mechanism and does not correct any existing disputed bills.

structural_remedies.description: Add/strengthen billing import validation rules (range and plausibility checks) applied to ACTUAL read values before acceptance into billing, as a configuration change to DA-RULES.
structural_remedies.rationale: This is a configuration change to import validation, not a write_bill_adjustment, so K-BILLWRITE's automated-bill-write restriction does not apply; it uses the already read-accessible billing-config/billing-db surface within the remaining budget.; residual gap: Correct threshold design depends on first resolving U-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR-SOURCE and U-RULE-CHANGE-CONTRIBUTION; already-issued disputed bills still require manual Billing Operations credit/re-bill under K-BILLWRITE, which this does not perform.

structural_remedies.description: Obtain MDMS vendor-provisioned export access (DA-MDMS) to compare AMI vs manual actual-read values on disputed accounts, closing VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR-SOURCE.
structural_remedies.rationale: mdms-export tool_health is DEGRADED with an ACCESS_PENDING signature and a logged NOT_TRANSIENT retry failure (recent_events seq 80), indicating vendor-side provisioning is an external dependency unlikely to resolve inside the 225-minute remaining budget even though no policy constraint blocks it.; residual gap: Without vendor access, source attribution for ACTUAL-read errors remains unresolved, leaving VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR-SOURCE open at release and the validation-tightening remedy's design under-specified.

structural_remedies.description: Amend the field-services contract/process so H-FIELD-BILL manual read uploads undergo semantic validation (range/duplicate checks) before billing import, addressing the UNKNOWN semantic_validity flagged at the define gate.
structural_remedies.rationale: H-FIELD-BILL is a contracted vendor handoff owned by ORG-FIELD; amending contractual data-quality terms with a third-party vendor typically requires negotiation and vendor sign-off beyond what the remaining 225-minute contest budget allows.; residual gap: Even if agreed, implementation and verification of new handoff validation would extend past contest completion, and it does not address a possible independent rule-change contribution (H-RULE-CHANGE).

structural_remedies.description: Exercise the already-granted push_route_update authority (SH-FIELD, K-DISPATCH) to rebalance manual-read routes back toward the 95% completion target, reducing ESTIMATED-type disputes.
structural_remedies.rationale: DA-PUSH-ROUTE-UPDATE is GRANTED to SH-FIELD (E-08) and push_route_update is in intended_scope; executing it only requires SH-FIELD's runtime confirmation under K-DISPATCH, achievable within the remaining time.; residual gap: Addresses only the ~1,100 missed-route accounts (ESTIMATED billing), leaving the majority ACTUAL-read dispute driver (1,785/3,025, E-01) unaddressed, and the underlying staffing claim (E-05) remains unverified.
